evidence.note: read health.doctor() (api/reporting/health.py) end to end; the slow run is a sequence of ~30 check calls with no per-check timing, on the 116MB log the per-ask transcript rescan (PS-doctor-onepass) is the known 76% cost

added [health].check_budget_s knob + _check/_over_budget_notes; doctor records check_timings + over_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The diff adds `_over_budget_notes`, but `doctor` never calls it. The only changes inside `doctor` are `with _check(...)` wrappers that append to `timings`; the existing `problems`/`notes` return path is unchanged. Therefore, if the configured per-check budget is 10s and a wrapped check such as `plan_for` takes 12s, `doctor` still returns no timing table and no “doctor check … over the … budget” note. The added helper can pass a direct unit test while the actual `doctor` command remains silent, so the stated regression/falsifier is not addressed.

chunk_findings.detail: The new timing helper uses `time.monotonic()` directly in reporting code. The project guidance says clocks are an external dependency and must go through a port/adapter in `ddflow/adapters`; importing and calling the real clock here bypasses that adapter boundary and couples `doctor` timing to the system clock instead of a single swappable/fakeable port.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `check_budget_s` knob documents that `ddflow doctor` “times each of its checks” and reports any single check exceeding the budget, but the shown doctor code times only `shared-files`, `progress`, `cleanup`, and `wait-cycles`; other finding-producing checks such as `found, held = _recovery_findings(L.scan(log, cfg, repo))`, `CL.unclaimed_trees`, `_untitled`, `_dupe_note`, `wait_order`, `LBR.doctor_notes`, and `cost.notes` are left untimed. Given a run where `L.scan` on the large log takes more than `check_budget_s` (default 60) while all wrapped checks are under 60, `_over_budget_notes(timings, cfg.health.check_budget_s)` sees no timed check over budget, returns `over=[]`, so `data["over_budget"]` is empty and no over-budget note is added even though a doctor check exceeded its budget.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_check_under_budget_is_not_reported` calls the real `embed` doctor check and asserts that it is not over budget, but it neither monkeypatches `EMB.doctor_notes` to a fast stub nor uses a fake clock. On a loaded or slow CI machine—the same kind of environment described in the intent, e.g. high load and slow disk—I/O or embedding work can make the real check exceed the default `[health].check_budget_s`. In that case `reporting.doctor` will correctly put an `embed` note in `out.data["over_budget"]`, and the assertion at line 44 fails even though the over-budget reporting logic is working. This makes the regression test nondeterministic; it should inject a controlled fast check or fake timing instead of relying on wall-clock performance of the real check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_over_budget_notes` helper is defined but is never called from `doctor` in the shown change. `doctor` builds and populates `timings`, but the diff does not pass `timings` to `_over_budget_notes` or append the resulting over-budget notes to `notes`. Given a doctor run where a timed check exceeds the configured budget (for example, `RP.integrity` takes 2s with a 1s budget), `doctor` returns without any “doctor check … over the … budget” note and the timing table is discarded, so the intended regression behavior does not occur.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_over_budget_notes

chunk_findings.detail: `doctor()` now records timings by wrapping `load`, `repairs.context`, `startcost`, `integrity`, `embed`, and `plan` with `_check`, but it never calls `_over_budget_notes` and never adds that function’s returned timing table or over-budget notes to the doctor report. Since `_over_budget_notes` is newly added in this same file and has no other caller, the production report path is unchanged: a run where `load` has a 200s timing and the configured budget is 120s still emits no per-check timing row and no over-budget note. The regression tests can import and pass `_over_budget_notes` directly while `doctor` remains silent, so the task’s over-budget reporting is not actually wired in.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:doctor

chunk_findings.detail: After `run_cli(repo, "init")`, the generated `.ddflow/config.toml` already contains a `[health]` table because `ddflow/config_sections/health.py` defines that config section and `ddflow init` writes the registered default sections. The test then appends a second `[health]` table with `check_budget_s = 1`. TOML forbids defining the same table twice, so the config parser will raise a `TOMLDecodeError` when `reporting.doctor` loads the config. This makes the over-budget regression test error out before it ever checks `check_timings` or `over_budget`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `check_budget_s` documentation promises that `ddflow doctor` “times each of its checks,” but the implementation only instruments a hardcoded subset of checks in `ddflow/api/reporting/health.py`. Several potentially expensive checks remain outside any `_check(...)` block, including `_rules_findings(...)` and `_launcher_findings(...)` around lines 436–438, `_driver_drift_notes`/`PM.driver_notes`/`PM.hook_notes` around line 441, `_unknown_author_notes` and `RP.doctor_notes` around lines 445–446, the `CL.unclaimed_trees` loop around line 457, `_untitled`, `_dupe_note`, and `cost.notes()` around line 474. If one of those untimed checks is the actual slow one on the 116 MB log — for example, if `RP.doctor_notes(...)` takes 10 minutes — then `timings` has no entry for it, `over_budget` remains empty, and `ddflow doctor` can still exceed 14 minutes while the new diagnostic reports that no check exceeded `check_budget_s`. That defeats the stated per-check timing/regression goal for any slow check not manually wrapped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_check_under_budget_is_not_reported` never configures `[health].check_budget_s`, so the test does not actually put the check under a known budget. It runs the real `embed` check and asserts it is not over budget based on whatever ambient/default budget and machine timing happen to be. On a loaded CI machine, cold filesystem, or with a default budget lower than the real embed check, the test can fail even when the over-budget feature is correct; with no default budget, the assertion can be vacuously true without exercising the under-budget path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The test file’s docstring promises that an over-budget check is reported “in `over_budget` (and as a note)”, but the test only checks that some `over_budget` entry contains the substring `"embed"`. It never asserts that the corresponding note is emitted or has the expected content, so a change that records `over_budget` but omits or corrupts the user-facing note would still pass this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: `_over_budget_notes` is defined but never called in `doctor` (or anywhere else in this file): `timings` is populated by `_check`, but after the wrapped calls it is not appended to `notes`, returned, or rendered. Running doctor on a log where one of the timed checks exceeds the configured budget therefore produces the same report as before: no “doctor check … over the budget” note and no timing table. The helpers and config can pass their tests while the user-visible falsifier remains true.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:doctor

chunk_findings.detail: The instrumentation does not cover all doctor work. For example `SM.accept(repo, log)` when `accept_lost_events` is true, `RULEVIEW.notes(repo, cfg, st)`, `OVR.notes(events, st, cfg)`, `AUD.findings(st, cfg)`, and `fold_problem_notes(st)` are executed without `_check`. On a log where one of those is the 14-minute consumer, there is no timing row for it, so the per-check budget table cannot name the slow check, contrary to the stated “timing every check” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:doctor

chunk_findings.detail: The new `check_budget_s` knob promises that “ddflow doctor times each of its checks” and records per-check timings, but several checks in this same function are still executed outside any `_check` context: `_rules_findings(repo, st.highest_version, problems, notes)`, `_launcher_findings(...)`, `PM.driver_notes(...)`, `RP.doctor_notes(...)`, and `CL.unclaimed_trees(...)`, among others. A repo with many workflow definitions or many worktrees can make one of those exceed the configured budget, yet it will produce no row in `check_timings` and no over-budget note at all. In that input the promised diagnostic output remains empty even though doctor blows its budget, so the change does not meet its own per-check timing promise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py `_rules_findings` and `_launcher_findings`

chunk_findings.detail: The over-budget test calls `run_cli(repo, "init")` and then appends a second `[health]` table to the generated `.ddflow/config.toml`. Since this change adds the `[health]` section via `ddflow/config_sections/health.py`, `ddflow init` emits a `[health]` table; the appended `[health]` table makes the TOML invalid because TOML forbids redefining a table. When `reporting.doctor` loads the config, Python 3.11+ `tomllib` raises `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`, so the regression test cannot reach the monkeypatch/timing assertions in the normal initialized repository.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous “under budget” fix does not make the test deterministic: it still runs the real `embed` check but sets `check_budget_s = 1`. If the real check takes longer than one second on a loaded CI runner, cold filesystem, or slower machine, `over_budget` will contain the `embed` entry and the final `assert not over` will fail even though the over-budget reporting is working correctly. The test should use a generous budget for the “not reported” case or stub/monkeypatch the check/duration; writing `check_budget_s = 1` only proves that the default budget was ambient, it does not guarantee the check is under budget.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `check_budget_s` documentation promises that `ddflow doctor` “times each of its checks,” but the implementation only instruments a hardcoded subset of checks in `ddflow/api/reporting/health.py`. Several potentially expensive checks remain outside any `_check(...)` block, including `_rules_findings(...)` and `_launcher_findings(...)` around lines 436–438, `_driver_drift_notes`/`PM.driver_notes`/`PM.hook_notes` around line 441, `_unknown_author_notes` and `RP.doctor_notes` around lines 445–446, the `CL.unclaimed_trees` loop around line 457, `_untitled`, `_dupe_note`, and `cost.notes()` around line 474. If one of those untimed checks is the actual slow one on the 116 MB log — for example, if `RP.doctor_notes(...)` takes 10 minutes — then `timings` has no entry for it, `over_budget` remains empty, and `ddflow doctor` can still exceed 14 minutes while the new diagnostic reports that no check exceeded `check_budget_s`. That defeats the stated per-check timing/regression goal for any slow check not manually wrapped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_check_under_budget_is_not_reported` never configures `[health].check_budget_s`, so the test does not actually put the check under a known budget. It runs the real `embed` check and asserts it is not over budget based on whatever ambient/default budget and machine timing happen to be. On a loaded CI machine, cold filesystem, or with a default budget lower than the real embed check, the test can fail even when the over-budget feature is correct; with no default budget, the assertion can be vacuously true without exercising the under-budget path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The test file’s docstring promises that an over-budget check is reported “in `over_budget` (and as a note)”, but the test only checks that some `over_budget` entry contains the substring `"embed"`. It never asserts that the corresponding note is emitted or has the expected content, so a change that records `over_budget` but omits or corrupts the user-facing note would still pass this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: `_over_budget_notes` is defined but never called in `doctor` (or anywhere else in this file): `timings` is populated by `_check`, but after the wrapped calls it is not appended to `notes`, returned, or rendered. Running doctor on a log where one of the timed checks exceeds the configured budget therefore produces the same report as before: no “doctor check … over the budget” note and no timing table. The helpers and config can pass their tests while the user-visible falsifier remains true.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:doctor

chunk_findings.detail: The instrumentation does not cover all doctor work. For example `SM.accept(repo, log)` when `accept_lost_events` is true, `RULEVIEW.notes(repo, cfg, st)`, `OVR.notes(events, st, cfg)`, `AUD.findings(st, cfg)`, and `fold_problem_notes(st)` are executed without `_check`. On a log where one of those is the 14-minute consumer, there is no timing row for it, so the per-check budget table cannot name the slow check, contrary to the stated “timing every check” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:doctor

chunk_findings.detail: The new `check_budget_s` knob promises that “ddflow doctor times each of its checks” and records per-check timings, but several checks in this same function are still executed outside any `_check` context: `_rules_findings(repo, st.highest_version, problems, notes)`, `_launcher_findings(...)`, `PM.driver_notes(...)`, `RP.doctor_notes(...)`, and `CL.unclaimed_trees(...)`, among others. A repo with many workflow definitions or many worktrees can make one of those exceed the configured budget, yet it will produce no row in `check_timings` and no over-budget note at all. In that input the promised diagnostic output remains empty even though doctor blows its budget, so the change does not meet its own per-check timing promise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py `_rules_findings` and `_launcher_findings`

chunk_findings.detail: The over-budget test calls `run_cli(repo, "init")` and then appends a second `[health]` table to the generated `.ddflow/config.toml`. Since this change adds the `[health]` section via `ddflow/config_sections/health.py`, `ddflow init` emits a `[health]` table; the appended `[health]` table makes the TOML invalid because TOML forbids redefining a table. When `reporting.doctor` loads the config, Python 3.11+ `tomllib` raises `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`, so the regression test cannot reach the monkeypatch/timing assertions in the normal initialized repository.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:28

chunk_findings.detail:
The helper still appends a second `[health]` table to `.ddflow/config.toml` after `ddflow init` has already generated the default config. Because this change ships a `[health]` config section (`ddflow/config_sections/health.py`), the generated config contains a `[health]` table; appending `"
[health]
check_budget_s = 1
"` creates a duplicate TOML table. On Python 3.11+, `tomllib` (used when loading the config) rejects duplicate table definitions, so both `test_a_check_over_its_budget_is_reported` and `test_a_check_under_budget_is_not_reported` can fail with `TOMLDecodeError` before the monkeypatched embed check or over-budget logic is exercised. The rewrite of the test did not remove the duplicate-table defect; it moved it into `_set_budget`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:_set_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion only verifies that *some* note contains the literal `"over the 1s per-check budget"`; it does not tie that note to the over-budget `embed` entry. If the implementation records `embed` in `out.data["over_budget"]` but fails to emit the corresponding user-facing note, the test still passes whenever any other un-stubbed, real check (e.g., `log-read` or `plan`) happens to exceed the 1-second budget on a loaded CI runner and produces the same phrase. The regression test therefore does not reliably fail when the falsifying bug — an over-budget check not reported to the user — occurs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doctor_time.py:45 (note assertion in `test_a_check_over_its_budget_is_reported`)
